driver: common/driver.cu: nearest_kernel<float><<<N=8, 1024>>>(x[N*2], y[M*2], ptr_x={0,N}, ptr_y={0,M}, out[N], batch_size=1, dim=2); args N M default 8 128; host brute-force reference prints mismatches.
input: 8 query points (one block each, as the 8-point example of test/test_nearest.py), ONE batch of M=128 reference points on a line, dim 2, query x = 0.25*q+0.1, y-points (M-j, 0) so the distance to every query decreases with j (the V minimum is at the last points): the in-place reduction then really executes the racy write at L54/L55 (writes only happen when best_dist[t] > best_dist[t+i], and thread w only holds a real distance for w < M). Deviation from the test's 4 reference points: with <= 64 references no thread w >= 32 ever executes the write, so no cross-warp pair would run; M=128 gives the cross-warp iteration i=32 (writers 32..95, readers 0..63) and intra-warp pairs for i=1..16. Thread-level access estimate (about 2e5, bound 3e5): per block 1024 threads x 10 iterations x 2 LDS + <= 3 more per executing lane + 2 STS per thread at the start + ~20 global accesses for the 128 distance threads, x 8 blocks.
